title: IRC logs / root
body:
^
        (
          # irssi / xchat and others
          (?: \[|\()?                  # Opening bracket or paren for the timestamp
            (?:                        # Timestamp
                (?: (?:\d{1,4} [-/])*  # Date as - or /-separated groups of digits
                    (?:\d{1,4})
                 [T ])?                # Date/time separator: T or space
                (?: \d?\d [:.])*       # Time as :/.-separated groups of 1 or 2 digits
                    (?: \d?\d)
            )
          (?: \]|\))?\s+               # Closing bracket or paren for the timestamp
        |
          # weechat
          \d{4}\s\w{3}\s\d{2}\s        # Date
          \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}\s+         # Time + Whitespace
        |
          # xchat
          \w{3}\s\d{2}\s               # Date
          \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}\s+         # Time + Whitespace
        )?
    (\s*<[^>]*>\s*)$ → <function bygroups.<locals>.callback at 0x000002A35B07EFC0>

                (.+?)                # anything, followed by:
                (?:
                 (?<=\n)(?=%|\#\#) | # an eval or comment line
                 (?=\#\*) |          # multiline comment
                 (?=</?%) |          # a python block
                                     # call start or end
                 (?=\$\{) |          # a substitution
                 (?<=\n)(?=\s*%) |
                                     # - don't consume
                 (\\\n) |            # an escaped newline
                 \Z                  # end of string
                )

title: HTTP action effects
body: HTTP distinguishes read-oriented safe methods from other operations. Idempotence concerns intended repeated effects, not absence of every incidental effect. Remote changes require checking service-specific results, retries and uncertain completion.
level: authored summary of primary documentation; not a complete world model

title: Causal processing traces
body: Traces follow requests across processing components. Metrics describe measured quantities; logs record events. Correlate identifiers and timestamps to inspect an action chain; correlation alone is not a causal experiment.
level: authored summary of primary documentation; not a complete world model

title: Windows process effects
body: Windows provides documented functions for process and thread creation, inspection and coordination. Predict effects from the exact operation, arguments, current rights and dependent processes; inspect actual completion before recording success.
level: authored summary of primary documentation; not a complete world model

title: Windows operating system profile
body: NT; Win32 and PowerShell; services and event logs; ACLs and access tokens; registry; driver/user-kernel boundary. Inspect exact Windows build and tool version before applying commands.
level: authored orientation; platform-specific verification required

title: Linux operating system profile
body: Kernel and distribution-specific user space; processes, file descriptors, POSIX permissions, capabilities, namespaces and cgroups; /proc and /sys. Service/package managers vary by distribution.
level: authored orientation; platform-specific verification required

title: macOS operating system profile
body: Darwin with Apple frameworks; launchd services; APFS; code signing, privacy permissions and system integrity controls. Linux commands and service assumptions are not interchangeable.
level: authored orientation; platform-specific verification required

title: Android operating system profile
body: Linux-based app platform; activities, services, broadcast receivers and content providers; manifest and runtime permissions; app identities and lifecycle. Developer tooling requires an actual connected authorised device.
level: authored orientation; platform-specific verification required

title: iOS and iPadOS operating system profile
body: Apple mobile app lifecycle, entitlements, app isolation, signing and privacy permissions. Desktop command access is not generally an app capability; use documented APIs and actual device permissions.
level: authored orientation; platform-specific verification required

title: Windows / process
body: Running program with identity, address space, resources and lifecycle. Inspect PID and executable; avoid confusing a reused PID with the original process. Platform-specific documentation and observed version are required.

title: Windows / thread
body: Execution stream sharing process resources; scheduling and concurrent mutation can affect outcomes. Platform-specific documentation and observed version are required.

body: Virtual address spaces, allocation, resident memory, paging and pressure differ; allocated bytes are not all available physical RAM. Platform-specific documentation and observed version are required.

body: Paths, permissions, case rules, links and atomic update semantics differ. Resolve exact targets and verify writes with readback. Platform-specific documentation and observed version are required.

title: Exact rational arithmetic
body: a/b + c/d = (ad+bc)/(bd); b and d nonzero. Exact integers/rationals avoid floating rounding; growth still needs resource bounds.
level: authored mathematical orientation; only registered solvers are executable

title: Bayesian updating
body: P(H|E)=P(E|H)P(H)/P(E), provided P(E)>0. Priors and likelihoods must be justified; repeated correlated sources are not independent evidence.
level: authored mathematical orientation; only registered solvers are executable

title: Information gain
body: Expected information gain compares entropy before and after a possible observation. Requires a defined hypothesis distribution and observation model; novelty alone is not information gain.
level: authored mathematical orientation; only registered solvers are executable

title: Causal intervention
body: An intervention changes a variable in an explicit causal model. Observational association, model projection and an actual intervention are distinct evidence types.
level: authored mathematical orientation; only registered solvers are executable

title: Queueing and throughput
body: Little's law L = lambda W relates average items in a stable system, arrival rate and waiting time. Consistent units and steady-state conditions matter.
level: authored mathematical orientation; only registered solvers are executable

title: Feedback control
body: A controller adjusts actions from measured error. Stability, delay, saturation and noise must be evaluated before increasing response rate.
level: authored mathematical orientation; only registered solvers are executable

title: Network graph flow
body: Flow conservation and capacity constraints model transport through graphs. Edges represent actual or hypothetical channels explicitly; a graph edge is not a network connection.
level: authored mathematical orientation; only registered solvers are executable

title: Constrained optimisation
body: Optimise an objective subject to explicit constraints and variable domains. An optimum is conditional on the objective and model; it is not a complete moral judgement.
level: authored mathematical orientation; only registered solvers are executable

title: Dimensional analysis
body: Only quantities of compatible dimensions can be added or compared directly. Preserve units, scale, uncertainty and measurement origin throughout calculations.
level: authored mathematical orientation; only registered solvers are executable

title: Energy and mass
body: E = mc^2 expresses rest energy. Numerical evaluation requires mass in compatible units and does not establish a mechanism to access that energy.
level: authored mathematical orientation; only registered solvers are executable

title: Quantum state evolution
body: The Schrodinger equation relates a state to a specified Hamiltonian. Boundary conditions, interactions and measurement model are required for predictions.
level: authored mathematical orientation; only registered solvers are executable

title: Cosmological expansion
body: H = a_dot/a defines expansion rate for a scale factor. Predictions depend on a cosmological model and observational parameter estimates.
level: authored mathematical orientation; only registered solvers are executable

title: Special functions and numerical accuracy
body: Choose algorithms according to parameter range, convergence and error bounds. Symbolic formulas may have numerical instability near singularities.
level: authored mathematical orientation; only registered solvers are executable
